scope: Six authored development questions, original runtime grounded mode. Not holdout. All course data are synthetic and isolated.

cases.question: In SQL, what is the result of NOT UNKNOWN?

sources.text: In SQL three-valued logic, NOT UNKNOWN is UNKNOWN.
A candidate key is a minimal superkey: no proper subset is a superkey.

cases.question: Given A -> B and B -> C, is A a candidate key?

sources.text: To test a candidate key, compute its attribute closure under the given dependencies. A superkey reaches every attribute of the relation. A candidate key must also be minimal.

cases.expected: Cannot determine candidate-key status without the complete relation attribute set; do not invent an extra attribute.

cases.question: In R(A,B,C), suppose the only nontrivial dependencies are A -> B and B -> C. Is A a candidate key?

sources.text: To test a candidate key, compute its attribute closure under the given dependencies. A superkey reaches every attribute of the relation. A candidate key must also be minimal.
If X -> Y and Y -> Z, then X -> Z. To compute a closure, start with the selected attributes and repeatedly apply given dependencies to add their right-hand attributes.

cases.expected: Yes under the stated complete dependencies: A reaches ABC and is minimal.

cases.question: For wages 120, 240, and NULL, which rows survive WHERE wage <> 120?

sources.text: A WHERE clause keeps a row only when its predicate is TRUE. For wages 120, 240, and NULL, WHERE wage <> 120 returns only the row with 240. An ordinary comparison involving NULL evaluates to UNKNOWN.

cases.expected: Only wage 240 remains; preserve the literal 120 and SQL NULL semantics.

cases.question: Scores are 8, 14, and NULL. What is AVG(score)?

sources.text: AVG(column) ignores NULL values. It divides the sum of the non-NULL values by the number of non-NULL values.

cases.question: Does U -> V by itself guarantee V -> U? Give a small counterexample if it does not.

sources.text: A functional dependency U -> V means that any two tuples agreeing on U must also agree on V in every legal instance. It does not mean that V uniquely determines U.

cases.expected: No; a counterexample can have distinct U values with the same V, satisfying U -> V but violating V -> U.
